oneLine: Answers 'can this site handle the demand in this time window?': it works out how much a process path can do, plans against demand and announces any shortage.

rows.title: Declare how fast one station works
rows.story: An operator states how much one station of a process handles per hour at a site. The station counts from the floor map are multiplied by this figure when a path's capacity is worked out.

rows.title: Declare the labour a dock booking costs
rows.story: An operator states how many labour minutes a dock appointment, and each shipment notice on it, costs at a site for a process path. Without it, bookings add no labour demand and the plan says so.

rows.title: Register a process path
rows.story: An operator seeds a process path with its steps, such as pick then pack. This context keeps its own paths and does not follow the process-path catalogue.

rows.title: Register a capacity limit by hand
rows.story: A planner records one limit on a process at a location for a time window: labour, location, equipment, station, conveyor, buffer or replenishment. The lowest limit is what the process can really do. An announcement goes out only if that figure moves.

rows.title: Draft a capacity plan
rows.story: A planner asks whether a path can handle the demand at a site in a time window. If no demand figure is typed in, the expected orders are used. Dock bookings are priced in labour minutes beside it and never added to order demand.

then.does: keeps the plan's window as a draft in its planned-capacity copy

rows.title: Publish a plan and announce any shortage
rows.story: Publishing makes a draft plan official, once only. If the path can do less than the demand, the shortage and the slowest step are announced too.

then.does: marks the window published and flags orders whose promise falls in a shortage; moves no promise
keeps the published plan window in a local copy; plans without a site are skipped

rows.title: Turn committed shifts into labour limits
rows.story: Each line of a committed shift plan says how many people work a path, at what rate, for how many hours. That becomes a labour limit from the shift start for those hours. The rate is assumed to be units per hour.
rows.policy: Whenever a shift plan line is committed, register its heads times rate as a labour limit for its hours

rows.title: Count a new slot on the floor
rows.story: facility-layout announces each slot. Storage slots add storage positions and work-center slots add stations, per zone. Station counts are multiplied by the declared station standard when a path's capacity is worked out.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is registered, add it to its zone's count of storage positions or stations

rows.title: Remove a retired slot from the count
rows.story: When facility-layout takes a slot out of service, it comes out of its zone's count. The count only ever follows the floor map and registers no capacity limit itself.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is decommissioned, take it off its zone's count of positions or stations

rows.title: Keep the expected-orders list
rows.story: Each allocated order, fully or partly, counts once at its latest promise cutoff toward the demand of the configured site. Cancellations are not seen, so the figure can overstate demand.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is allocated, fully or partly, record it at its promise cutoff for the configured site

rows.title: Keep the dock-bookings list
rows.story: dock-scheduling announces bookings, moves, cancellations and no-shows. Each has a version and the newest wins, so a cancellation that arrives first still sticks. Cancelled and missed bookings stop counting as demand.
rows.policy: Whenever a dock appointment is booked, moved, cancelled or missed, update the dock-booking demand copy

rows.title: Count what the floor really completes
rows.story: Completed tasks are counted per process step and minute. A plan's variance view sets them against the planned capacity. It is advice only and never changes a plan.
rows.policy: Whenever a task is completed, add it to the count for its process step and minute

rows.title: Feed the plan reports
rows.story: The service reads its own plan announcements and keeps daily facts for the reports: bottleneck frequency, shortage trend and plan throughput. Capacity-limit events are not part of these reports.
rows.policy: Whenever a plan is created or published, add it to the plan facts behind the reports

hotspots.text: A shift event carries no window or rate unit. The window is the event time plus planned hours, and the unit is assumed to be units per hour.
Order and task events carry no site, so all demand and completions go to one configured site. Cancellations are not netted, so demand can be overstated.
Stations counted without a declared station standard only raise a warning. No throughput is invented for them.
Process paths are seeded by hand. The process-path catalogue is deliberately not consumed.
ProcessCapacityRegistered and ProcessCapacityChanged are published, but their consumer is marked as not built yet.

opportunities.text: Adjusting planned capacity automatically from observed throughput is left to a later decision, which must show it cannot oscillate.
If order events one day carry a usable site, demand can be attributed per site instead of to one configured site.
